original_question: Develop effective mathematical techniques for computing higher-genus Gromov-Witten invariants of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds.
target_in_paper: Q9 in section (iv) On the moduli of K3 surfaces: "Find effective mathematical methods for calculating the higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds."
correct_elements: Your draft already tracks the paper's target extremely closely: it asks for effective mathematical methods/techniques, it is explicitly about higher-genus Gromov-Witten invariants, and it keeps the scope to compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds rather than broadening to other geometries or to a different enumerative theory.
missing_details: The nearest official formulation is exactly Q9, phrased as "Find effective mathematical methods for calculating..."; the paper does not frame this as a broader conjectural program or as a problem about all Calabi-Yau targets.

The paper uses "higher genus" informally; the surrounding discussion contrasts this problem with genus-0 progress and cites genus 1 as an example, so the intended scope is positive-genus Gromov-Witten theory rather than genus 0.

The intended meaning of "effective" is contextual: the paper contrasts the desired methods with existing "complete, but less effective" techniques for the quintic and notes that the holomorphic anomaly equation was, at that time, more effective than the available mathematical methods.

Q9 is asked immediately after Q8; the paper explains that proving the Katz-Klemm-Vafa conjecture for all genera and classes on K3 surfaces would already yield exact formulas for a large class of higher-genus Gromov-Witten invariants of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds.

No additional ambient ring/field, operator, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or "for all sufficiently large m" conditions appear in Q9; the problem is intentionally open-ended and does not impose a specific curve class, genus bound, or family of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds.
refined_question: Find effective mathematical methods for calculating the higher-genus Gromov-Witten invariants of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds.
justification: The draft is essentially a restatement of Q9 and is closer to Q9 than to the neighboring Q8. Q8 is specifically about proving the Katz-Klemm-Vafa conjecture for all genera and all classes on K3 surfaces, whereas your draft does not mention K3 surfaces, reduced K3 theory, or K3-fiber classes. The nearby context explains why Q9 appears here: the paper notes that a solution to Q8 would already provide exact formulas for a large class of higher-genus invariants of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds, but then isolates the broader methodological problem in Q9 itself. The sentences following Q9 clarify the paper's intended benchmark for effectiveness by contrasting existing effective low-genus calculations for the Enriques Calabi-Yau, complete but less effective methods for the quintic, and the comparatively stronger practical effectiveness of the holomorphic anomaly equation.
